item.title: Bhagat Singh, Knife grinder, maker and locksmith, Patiala - Trolley Times
item.description: These shops (around Qila Mubaarak) used to be stables of royal horses. They changed into shops as the monarchs left the fort. My father and grandfather used to work as mechanics for Maharaja Bhupinder Singh and on the side they would bring Sikh kakaars (steel bangles and wooden combs) from Amritsar and sell them in Patiala

item.title: Baljit Singh, Carpenter, Mohali - Trolley Times
item.description: We are carpenters from 15 generations. Our ancestors worked for 'the Sodhis' of Ferozpur. It was the honesty of my people that appealed to them. We were to take care of their agricultural machines and daily needs.

item.title: Ranjit Singh, Blacksmith, Daun - Trolley Times
item.description: Machines can never replace what's done with hands. All this repair work you see, this fine finishing with these tools is handwork, there's no machine you can place it under and get such results. I've been here for 35 years and I don't think I will leave soon.

item.title: Sociology of grief and politics of death in Sidhu Moose Wala’s case -
item.description: The sea of people mourning the sudden demise of Sidhu Moose Wala was noted at Bhog ceremony, where people from different states, ages, gender, caste, class, political affiliations, and ideologies participated.

item.title: "And the blocking of the road continues..." -The Dutch farmers' protest - Trolley Times
item.description: Even after the historic defeat of the fascist government in India, the neoliberal order has been none the wiser. item.title: “When relentless struggle of sanitation workers comes to a victorious end..” - Trolley Times
item.description: The joint struggle of various unions started from the 1st of july across the state of Karnataka. There was a call for complete strike by sanitation workers (Powrakarmikara) that includes women workers who sweep the road and male workers who take the charge of collecting garbage and transporting it to the dumping yard; all the workers are predominantly dalits.

item.title: Budha Dariya: From a river to a drain of toxic water - Trolley Times
item.description: It is a tradition in the Punjabi language to call old courses or tributaries of rivers, Budha(Old) or Purana(Ancient). An old course of river Ravi was called Budha Dariya. A tributary that originated from the Satluj bay near Ropar town is also called Budha or Purana Dariya. This tributary fell into Ghaggar river near Moonak(Patiala district), but then it started flowing parallel to the Ghaghar.

item.title: Jal, Jungle, Zameen: lived realities of displaced Shariya tribe - Trolley Times
item.description: “I do not want to do agriculture, but I have to feed myself and my family. I have given ITI exams; I wish I could get a government job, but there are no jobs. I cannot take coaching like rich people to get a job”. This is Ramesh; he belongs to the Shariya Adivasi community […]

item.title: Toiling for the bare minimum: A story of Andhra’s farmers - Trolley Times
item.description: A friend sadly says, “the plight of the masses being displaced from their homes, and their fears about rehabilitation are often disregarded in cases involving land acquisitions for development”.

item.title: ਹਰੀ ਕ੍ਰਾਂਤੀ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀਆਂ ਜੜ੍ਹਾਂ ਚ ਬਹਿ ਗਈ - Trolley Times
item.description: The article discusses the legacy of M.S. Swaminathan, often hailed as the architect of the Green Revolution in India. While international recognition credits him with transforming Indian agriculture and combating famine, the author argues that the Green Revolution had severe consequences, particularly in Punjab.
